name: C2SIM_AggregateTacticalLevel
status: DESIGN 2026-09-27 (package C2, lane feat/aggregate-authored-units; RL-20260927-04 under RL-20260927-02). NOT live-proven: no VR-Forces run has loaded these types.
readme: THE DECISIONS for the authored US Army aggregate unit types. tools/aggregate/authored_units.py --write turns this file into tools/sms/C2SIM_AggregateTacticalLevel.recipe.json (literal, asserted edits); tools/sms/Deploy-C2SimAggregateSms.ps1 applies the recipe to the INSTALLED vendor files and writes C:\C2SIM\vrf-sms\C2SIM_AggregateTacticalLevel.sms + its directory. No vendor file is in the repo.

CONSTRUCTION RULE (every type): donor = the vendor .entity whose NON-rolled parameters (platform, movement system and its terrain class, sensors, enabler / weapon / engineering systems, postures, sectors, modifiers, supply structure) fit the US unit. assemblies = the FM 3-96 sub-elements, each as the vendor's own US assembly, rolled up by the vendor's rules (UG52 72.5 p1428; tools/aggregate/authored_units.py --selftest proves the port on the vendor's units). A variable no authored assembly supplies keeps the donor's value (72.5: 'Any parameters that are not part of an assembly or roll up rules do not change'); --report lists them per type. set = explicit decisions after the roll-up, each with its reason. systems = whole donor system blocks deleted, or grafted from another vendor .entity, where doctrine requires it.

Personnel and equipment are REPORTING ONLY - 'not used by the sim engine in the simulation' (UG52 72.7.9 p1438; 27.1 p528). They are rolled up from the same assemblies (plus the vendor's Officer+/NCO+/Enlisted+ personnel assemblies where the vendor's own US templates use them) and UNDER-count an MTOE: an owner item, not a sim defect.

Doctrine: FM 3-96 Brigade Combat Team, HQDA, 19 January 2021, chapter 1, paragraph numbers as cited; FM 3-94 Armies, Corps, and Division Operations, HQDA, 23 July 2021, paragraphs 5-22 and 5-23 (division headquarters). Vendor: VR-Forces 5.2 Users Guide (UG52) as cited.

DIS object types: kind 11 (MilitaryHierarchy), domain 1, country 225, category = echelon (UG52 D.3.4 p1689-1690: 6 Battalion), subcategory = the branch (D.3.4 Unit Subcategory p1690, 'the Echelon Type of the unit'; 31 is not in that list - it is the value the vendor's own US CSS units carry, CSS CO (USA) 11:1:225:5:31:1:1), specific 1 = ContainsHeadquarters (D.3.5 p1690), extra = a unique id in 201-207 ('the extra enumerated field provides a way to uniquely identify all objects', D.3.1 p1688). matchType = objectType exactly, so an authored template answers only its own type: it never captures an init-shell or container query (those use specific/extra 1:0 or 1:1).

header: ;; C2SIM_AggregateTacticalLevel.sms - C2SIM derived AGGREGATE-LEVEL simulation model set (VRF_C2SIM repo).
;; GENERATED by tools/sms/Deploy-C2SimAggregateSms.ps1 from the installed VR-Forces files and
;; tools/sms/C2SIM_AggregateTacticalLevel.recipe.json. Do not edit; rerun the script.
;; Body = the vendor AggregateTacticalLevel.sms with model-set-directory changed and its include retargeted
;; to AggregateTacticalLevel.sms itself (UG52 68.3.1 p1310, 68.3.3 p1312). This set only ADDS: the authored
;; US unit types (vrfSim\*.entity, UG52 68.8 p1326) and their unit symbols (gui\visuals\Unit, 68.5.4 p1320).

replace.why: this set's own directory, beside the .sms (the layout of every C2SIM derived set)
include the shipped AggregateTacticalLevel.sms UNCHANGED; the including set has the higher priority (UG52 68.3.3 p1312)

equipmentToEntityLevel.Truck w/trailer: M1083 MTV Cargo Truck w_ trailer.entity

types.label: Infantry BN (USA, IBCT)
assemblies: FM 3-96 1-7 three rifle companies x 1-8 three rifle platoons x (three rifle squads + one weapons squad); the vendor's US Army squad (2 NCO, 6 enlisted, Javelin)
1-8: each rifle company's mortar section, two 60-mm
1-7: the HHC mortar platoon's 120-mm mortars; four tubes as in the vendor's US mortar platoon (Mortar PLT (USA, M1064): 4 x M1064)
1-9: two ITAS vehicles in each of the four assault platoons
1-9: one MK19 weapon vehicle per assault platoon
1-9: one M2 weapon vehicle per assault platoon
1-9: the leader's vehicle of each assault platoon
the nine rifle platoon leaders (1-8), the mortar platoon leader (vendor Mortar PLT (USA, M1064): 1) and the BN staff (vendor BN-staff device of Engineering BN (POL): 3)
weapons company squad leaders 16 (1-9: 16 squads), mortar platoon 3 (vendor Mortar PLT (USA, M1064)), BN staff 6 (vendor device)
weapons company crews 48 (1-9: four Soldiers per squad, less the squad leader), mortar platoon 8 (vendor Mortar PLT (USA, M1064)), BN staff 12 (vendor device)

max-speed.why: the IBCT fights dismounted (FM 3-96 1-1, 1-5, 1-6): maximum speed of the vendor's US foot infantry (Rifle PLT (USA, USMC))

ordered-speed.why: ordered speed of the vendor's US foot infantry (Rifle PLT (USA, USMC))

Base-Diesel-Fuel.why: the donor's diesel is its Rosomak fleet's; the authored vehicles are the vendor's HMMWV assemblies, which roll up motor gas

Diesel-Fuel-Usage-Per-Meter.why: as Base-Diesel-Fuel: no diesel vehicle in the authored unit

can-be-embarked-upon.why: a foot battalion carries no other unit (the vendor's US Rifle PLT (USA, USMC) value)

replaceFrom.why: IBCT infantry moves on foot (FM 3-96 1-1, 1-5): the vendor's US foot movement system (infantry-aggregated-movement: MAK_WATERWAY impassable). The donor's amphibious system SWIMS water (featureconfig.txt: MAK_AMPHIBIOUS_RESTRICTED_L2_TERRAIN includes MAK_WATERWAY)

leaf.why: the vendor's US infantry symbol (outline glyph 17137)

provenance.doctrine: FM 3-96 1-6 (three Infantry battalions are the IBCT's primary maneuver forces), 1-7 (HHC, three rifle companies, weapons company; HHC mortar platoon 120-mm), 1-8 (rifle company: three rifle platoons of three rifle squads + a weapons squad, mortar section of two 60-mm), 1-9 (weapons company: four assault platoons, 2 ITAS + MK19/M2 vehicles, four Soldiers per squad)
provenance.donorWhy: Motorized BN (POL, Rosomak): a NATO battalion-level infantry unit whose systems are exactly an infantry battalion's - 120-mm mortar tube (1-7), ground-unit-tactics-enabler (attack / defend / march tasks), simple obstacle destroyer, reports, IR / engineering / NBC sensors - with no SAM and no engineer systems, and a battalion footprint (2000 m). Mech CO (USA, M2) scaled was rejected: a company-level footprint and posture set, tracked movement, no tactics enabler of a battalion. Its mobility is replaced (foot, above).
provenance.scale: roll-up of vendor US assemblies: health = 9 x the vendor's USMC rifle platoon (Rifle PLT (USA, USMC) 2262) within 10 pct; the vendor's light infantry company scale (Airmobile Rifle CO (RUS) 6000) x 3

types.label: FA BN (USA, IBCT)
assemblies: FM 3-96 1-12: two 105-mm firing batteries of six M119
1-12: one 155-mm firing battery of six M777 (the vendor's US towed 155-mm assembly)
one HMMWV per gun section, the vendor's US towed-artillery pattern (FA PLT (USA, 155mm): 2 guns, 2 HMMWV, 2 trucks); prime mover of the M119
prime mover of each M777 (the same vendor pattern)
1-12: the target acquisition platoon's counterbattery radar (the SMS's US radar key)

Base-Combat-Power-Anti-Air-Strength.why: FM 3-96 1-12 gives the IBCT FA battalion no organic air defense; the donor's 96 is the Lithuanian batteries' MANPADS (FA BTY (LTU, 105mm) assembly: 32 each)

Base-Combat-Power-Anti-Tank-Strength.why: the donor's 54 is the Lithuanian batteries' RPG-7s; no authored US assembly carries an anti-tank weapon or its ammunition (the vendor's US FA PLT (USA, 155mm) has anti-tank strength 0)

Base-Combat-Power-High-Explosive-Strengt.why: the donor's 9 is the Lithuanian AGS-17s; as anti-tank (the vendor's US FA PLT has high-explosive strength 0 - indirect fire is the howitzer SYSTEMS, not this strength)

Base-Diesel-Fuel.why: the donor's diesel is its Lithuanian trucks'; the authored HMMWV/Truck assemblies roll up motor gas

Base-Personnel-Officers.why: REPORTING ONLY (UG52 72.7.9): per gun the vendor's US FA platoon strength (FA PLT (USA, 155mm): 3/27/26 for two guns) x 9, plus the BN staff 3/6/12

insertFrom.why: FASCAM (ADAM/RAAM), as the vendor's US 155-mm platoon carries it, for the M777 battery (1-12)
the 155-mm howitzer system of the M777 battery (1-12), the vendor's US block unchanged (strength 800, sheaf 80: the vendor keeps per-system values in battalions)

leaf.why: the vendor's towed field-artillery symbol (outline glyph 17329)

provenance.doctrine: FM 3-96 1-12: HHB, two 105-mm batteries (six-gun M119), one 155-mm battery (six-gun M777), two 3-gun platoons per battery, a target acquisition platoon (counterbattery and countermortar radars)
provenance.donorWhy: FA BN (LTU, 105mm): the vendor's towed 105-mm battalion (NATO) - motorized movement for towed guns, the 105-mm howitzer system, the artillery-automatic-attack enabler (automatic fire support) and the tactics enabler. The 155-mm battery's systems are grafted from the vendor's US FA PLT (USA, 155mm).
provenance.scale: roll-up: health within 30 pct of the donor's (FA BN (LTU, 105mm) 6510 for 18 guns)

delete.why: bridge-builder: 'The IBCT currently does not have a bridging capability and requires augmentation from echelons above brigade engineers' (FM 3-96 1-19)
consumed only by bridge building, which the IBCT BEB has not got (FM 3-96 1-19)

provenance.doctrine: FM 3-96 1-13 (HHC, two engineer companies, signal company, MI company with TUAS platoon, CBRN recon platoon), 1-17 (mobility, countermobility, survivability: breach, obstacles, survivability positions, route clearance), 1-18 (company A: combat engineer platoons, engineer support platoon; IBCT mine clearing line charges), 1-19 (company B adds route clearance; IBCT breach = MICLIC, NO bridging)
provenance.donorWhy: Engineering BN (POL): the vendor's wheeled engineer battalion (motorized movement, as the IBCT's wheeled BEB), carrying the aggregate engineering systems the breach and obstacle tasks need - obstacle-builder, ditch-digger, fortification-builder, mine-dispenser, engineering-obstacle-destroyer (breach) - and the construction-material, explosives, mine-canister and concertina supplies they consume (UG52 27.2.3 p536; 72.7.10 p1438). Engineer BN (RUS, Mech) is the ABCT donor (tracked).
provenance.scale: NO roll-up: the SMS has no US engineer assembly, so the donor's own roll-up stands (three engineer companies + staff, health 17580) for the BEB's two engineer companies + signal / MI / CBRN / HHC elements; equipment replaced by US vehicles (reporting only)

types.label: Brigade Support BN (USA)
assemblies: FM 3-96 1-27: the distribution company - the vendor's US CSS company (24 trucks)
1-27: the field maintenance company's repair vehicles (the SMS's US repair assembly)
1-27: the field maintenance company's recovery vehicles
1-27: the Role 2 medical company's ambulances (the SMS's US ambulance assembly)

provenance.doctrine: FM 3-96 1-27: command group and staff, six forward support companies (one per battalion / squadron, normally in direct support), a distribution company, a field maintenance company and a Role 2 medical company; the SBCT and ABCT BSB has the same general configuration, the main difference is maintenance
provenance.donorWhy: Logistics BN (LTU): the vendor's battalion-level logistics unit - the resupplier system that makes a unit a supply source (UG52 27.3.2 p539: resupplier.sysdef; 'it never runs out'), motorized movement, a battalion footprint (2000 m). CSS CO (USA) carries the same systems at company level and is used as the distribution-company assembly.
provenance.scale: roll-up without the six FSCs (they support the battalions forward; not in this leaf - an owner item): health above the donor's (Logistics BN (LTU) 6600) and below Logistics BN (POL) 17760

types.label: Division HQ (USA)
assemblies: FM 3-94 5-22: main, tactical and rear command posts - two command-post carriers each (the SMS's US command-post assembly, M577)
FM 3-94 5-23: the HHB companies' light vehicles
FM 3-94 5-23: the HHB's life support and transportation
FM 3-94 5-23 'a complete battalion staff' (vendor BN-staff device)

Base-Physical-Footprint.why: the vendor's brigade HQ units occupy 1000 m (Mech BDE HQ (RU, BMP-3), Tank BDE HQ (RUS, T-90)); the donor troop's 300 m is a squadron HQ troop

insertFrom.why: a headquarters: the vendor's HQ enabler (manage-fire-support), as the vendor's US Tank BN HQ carries it; the donor troop has none

provenance.doctrine: FM 3-96 chapter 1 introduction p1-1 (the division is the tactical headquarters over two to five BCTs); FM 3-94 5-22 (the division headquarters and headquarters battalion: main, tactical and rear command posts, a mobile command group), 5-23 (HHB: complete battalion staff, HQ and support company, signal / intelligence / sustainment company). DIS category 6: the unit IS a battalion (the HHB), the vendor's HQ units sit below their formation (BN HQ at PLT, BDE HQ at CO), and UG52 40.80 p902 requires the superior (the division container) to be a higher echelon.
provenance.donorWhy: Stryker HHT (USA): the vendor's US wheeled headquarters unit (motorized movement, tactics enabler). Tank BN HQ (USA, M1A2) was rejected as the body (tracked tank movement, two M1A2); its headquarters enabler is grafted.
provenance.scale: roll-up: health about 1.4 x the vendor's Tank BDE HQ (RUS, T-90) 6860

the Paladin section's ammunition carrier, one per howitzer (not in FM 3-96; the vendor pairs M992 with M109A6 in its US assemblies)

HHB / FDC vehicles (estimate; FM 3-96 gives no count)

Base-Combat-Power-High-Explosive-Strengt.why: the donor's 54 is the Polish battalion's; indirect fire is the howitzer SYSTEM, not this strength (the vendor's US FA PLT has high-explosive strength 0)

Base-Personnel-Officers.why: REPORTING ONLY (UG52 72.7.9): per gun the vendor's US FA platoon strength (FA PLT (USA, 155mm): 3/27/26 for two guns) x 9, plus the BN staff 3/6/12

delete.why: the 9K38 SAM of the Polish battalion; FM 3-96 1-44 gives the ABCT FA battalion no organic air defense

provenance.doctrine: FM 3-96 1-44: HHB and three batteries of six M109 Paladin 155-mm SP howitzers, two firing platoons of three guns per battery; two AN/TPQ-53 and four AN/TPQ-50 radars
provenance.donorWhy: SP Artillery BN (POL, K9): the vendor's NATO 155-mm self-propelled battalion (K9, the M109's class) - tracked mech movement, the 155-mm howitzer and FASCAM systems, the automatic-attack and tactics enablers.
provenance.scale: roll-up: health within 10 pct of the donor's (18200)

provenance.doctrine: FM 3-96 1-13 (BEB organization), 1-18 (company A identical in IBCT and ABCT; Armored BCTs have rapidly emplaced bridges and Volcano), 1-19 (the ABCT breach section consists of bridging), 1-39 (engineers organic to the ABCT)

Kept whole.
